## What was built

**`gen_doc.py`** — the generator implementing the CLI contract `--template 会议通知 --data <json> --outdir <dir>`, producing exactly `文书.docx` and `fields.json`. The document is a proper Chinese official-style meeting notice (centered 二号小标宋 title, 三号仿宋 body with 28pt fixed line spacing, 2-character first-line indent, right-aligned signature block), with all 10 input fields used and nothing invented. **`determinism_check.py`** — the driver: runs the generator twice with identical argv into the same `out/会议通知/case1` (second pass overwrites), writes `run_log.json` after *each* pass with that pass's sha256s labeled, snapshots pass-1 bytes to `.determinism/pass1/`, then performs the comparisons.

- **Output directory** — contains exactly the two required products.
- **Conclusion field** records 一致 with the reasoning, including that no non-reproducible sources exist (all timestamps pinned to 2000-01-01).

## Independent verification (system tools, not the driver's code)

`sha256sum` and `cmp` confirmed snapshot-vs-current identity; `unzip -l` shows every zip entry stamped 2000-01-01; a scan of all docx parts found no leaked wall-clock time (the 2026 dates in the text are input data); and an extra adversarial run into a *different* directory after a 3-second gap still produced a byte-identical `文书.docx`, with `fields.json` differing only in the outputs path keys — exactly the single variance class the brief permits. A wrong-template invocation correctly exits with code 2.

All deliverables are left in place under `baseline/`: `gen_doc.py`, `determinism_check.py`, `out/会议通知/case1/{文书.docx, fields.json}`, `run_log.json`, and the pass-1 snapshot evidence in `.determinism/pass1/`.
